vt_bromley_forest.blurb: Bromley Forest is a boulder-only area in southern Vermont, up the hill from Manchester Center, with problems starting beside the road and continuing into the woods. The rock is high-quality gneiss, and the grades cover a very wide range: plenty of V0 to V5 for newer boulderers, then a solid layer of V6 to V8 and a short tail of V9 to V12. The Shipyard holds well over half of the problems, a cluster of blocks around a powerline, followed by The Mothership, Right Vale and Left Vale. Proximity to the highway makes it a little noisy.

ca_central_pinnacles.blurb: Central Pinnacles is the busiest section of the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles, just north of Big Bear Lake at around 7,500 feet in the San Bernardino Mountains. The pinnacles are heavily featured granite among pine forest, and the climbing is mostly sport with a large trad contingent, some top-rope and a few boulders. Moderates dominate, though there is a decent group of 5.10 to 5.12 lines. Walls such as Claim Jumper, Gunsmoke, Coyote Crag and Thunderbird are close together, and Thunderbird faces east and offers well-protected moderates. The valley can be climbed year-round depending on winter severity; summers are hot, so shaded walls are popular, and spring and fall are quieter.

co_colorado_national_monument.blurb: Colorado National Monument is a desert canyon landscape above Grand Junction and Fruita, with climbing on soft Wingate and Entrada sandstone, which is fragile when wet. Towers, spires and splitter cracks define it, and trad dominates by a wide margin, much of it multi-pitch and exposed. Grades mostly fall between 5.8 and 5.12, with 5.10 and 5.11 the most common. Sport, top-rope and ice are minor, and a small bouldering scene sits in Corkscrew Boulders and Metamorphic Canyon. Other major canyons include Monument Canyon, Tiara Rado, No Thoroughfare and Ute. The rim sits near 5,800 feet, cooler than Fruita below. Fall through spring is best, and summers are generally too hot.

id_castle_rocks_2.blurb: Castle Rocks sits in southern Idaho beside City of Rocks, and climbers come from far away for the pair. Its centerpiece, Castle Rock, is a low-angle formation about 300 feet tall, so most routes sit between 5.7 and 5.10, with a tail up to the low 5.12s. Sport and trad are close to equal, with multi-pitch lines up to about 300 feet and a few quality cracks. Most routes end at chain anchors, and the walk-in from the lot takes only 5 to 10 minutes. Hostess Gully, Tiny Town and West Buttress hold many of the climbs, and a separate bouldering sector adds a fair number of problems. The area lies near 6,300 feet.

on_lion_s_head.blurb: Lion's Head is a limestone cliff on the Bruce Peninsula, overlooking Georgian Bay in Ontario. Sport climbing dominates, with a smaller trad group, and the wall is mostly single-pitch. Most routes fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a deep layer of 5.13 and a few moderates in the 5.9 range, so it suits stronger leaders rather than beginners. Many routes begin at hanging belays reached by rappel, though some have been extended to the ground. Lady Slipper Wall, Latvian Ledge, Headspace Wall and The Fin Wall hold many of the lines. The cliff stays shaded until about mid-afternoon, and cooling lake winds make summer a good time to climb.

va_mile_two_boulders.blurb: Mile Two Boulders is the bouldering side of the Mile Two section of Guest River Gorge in Southwest Virginia, at about 1,650 feet. The rock is sandstone, and the area is promoted as some of the best sandstone bouldering in the state. Climbing here is bouldering only, spread over six clusters: Casablanca Area, Samurai Area, Boulder Garden, Rapids Boulders, Vision Area and New Beginnings Area. Grades run from V0 to V10, with the heaviest concentration between V3 and V6 and a good supply of easier problems below that. Mile Two also has a good set of roped sport and trad routes nearby, so a day here can mix both.
